overall_assessment: All 28 courses were reviewed, including 11 suspects. Extraction generally preserves the available plan and readable structure: uncaptured flags reflect excluded staff/contact boxes, next-term links or alternative link serialization; the three short suspects are sparse or expired/pointer source pages, and the visible junk-flagged blockchain plan contains legitimate subject matter rather than demonstrated site chrome. The major discrepancy is that all 28 pages are labelled absent page shells although 25 contain substantive plans; current-plan year differences are expected, and the packet/build provenance must be reconciled before attributing those absences to extraction.

findings.evidence: - Plan in the build: **none**: a page shell (no section, under 1500 chars of plan text)
findings.description: The stated no-plan reason contradicts the page contents for 25 of 28 courses, including all 17 random controls. For example, BAN427 has 4295 characters with topics, learning outcomes, teaching, assessment and literature; FIE420 has 3129 characters with the corresponding Norwegian sections; TECH3 has 5332 characters with a detailed plan. These are not facts-only page shells. This finding concerns the incorrect no-plan decision or its reported reason, as required by the rubric; it does not establish that the shell filter actually removed these pilot pages. BAN402 and CEMSBS are genuinely sparse, and SOL23 is an expired English-page pointer. Other text defects on pages marked dropped are not separate findings.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/audit/prepare_fulltext.R joins pilot_run_rows() to processed build_plans by course_id, then no_plan_reason() defaults to a shell explanation without checking .shell_plans(), actual sections or plan_nchar. R/audit/utils.R documents that current-plan pilot pages are associated with the original DBH offerings while read_harvest() assigns them only to the page academic year. Thus a 2026/27 pilot page may be compared with an unrelated 2025 build absence; the packet alone cannot establish an actual shell-filter defect.
findings.suggested_fix: For current-plan pilot audits, trace the same fetched page through its actual build academic-year assignment before reporting plan availability. Make no_plan_reason() use recorded build exclusion provenance and emit the shell reason only when the relevant page has no sections and plan_nchar is below SHELL_MAX_NCHAR. Represent a pilot page with no matching build page explicitly instead of inferring a shell, then regenerate the packet; if matching substantive pages really fail the shell test, inspect their facts flags and section extraction before rebuilding.
